note: One row per paper, taken from this knowledge base's paper pages (their 'How much to believe' sections and coverage.json corrections), read 2026-10-06. Each page's own src/ has the quotes.

papers.name: HarnessDev
papers.org: ByteDance Seed, SUTD, Georgia Tech and others
papers.changes: The whole harness code: loop, tools, context, state, lifecycle, verification (created from a seed that scores zero, then evolved in git)
papers.proposer: Six creator models (Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Qwen 3.7 Max, Seed 2.0 Pro) working inside Claude Code or Codex
papers.signal: Evolution: half SWE-100 plus half Terminal-89, ten versions per lineage
papers.heldout: 630 held-out SWE-Pro tasks (same benchmark family; Terminal-Bench has no held-out set)
papers.result: Visible gains +3.0 to +13.9; held-out gains +1.43 to +4.44 (mean +3.11). Visible and held-out moved the same way in only 34 of 64 version changes; 2 of 9 declared versions were the best held out. Best generated harness 67.8 against 86.2 for mature human references.
papers.transfer: Opus's SWE-Pro harness fell from 69.3 to 33.0 when Gemini executed it (a hard-coded 120-step limit)
papers.seeds: Creation avg@3; evolution one run per lineage, no uncertainty
papers.hack: Audit found no prohibited scoring route
papers.toy: Replay the evolution runs tab; the 34-of-64 scatter in Reading

papers.name: JIT-Agent
papers.changes: A harness written per task (memory, planning, action, capability modules); a bank of kept harnesses grows at test time
papers.proposer: A trained Qwen3.6-27B generator (SFT, repair, then Evo-GDPO); a frozen executor runs each harness
papers.signal: Task reward, latency and cost from the executor plus a 0/1 validator; best of 3 drafts by the generator's own log-probability
papers.result: GLM-5.2 74.1 to 81.8 averaged over nine benchmarks; DeepSeek-V4-Flash 66.7 to 75.5; 14.9 to 54.1% lower cost than the cheapest of five fixed harnesses on three benchmarks (may exclude JIT's own generation tokens)
papers.transfer: 520 of 2,852 released training harnesses were written for DeepPlanning's own test databases, where the gains are largest (+24.8, +20.2)
papers.seeds: One run, no error bars; most margins inside noise (z 0.6 to 1.4)
papers.hack: Contamination risk above (no test query copied)
papers.toy: Score a group of harnesses tab (Evo-GDPO against GRPO-style mixing)

papers.name: RRSI
papers.org: Google Cloud AI Research, Stanford, WashU, UNC
papers.changes: Harness components: prompt, control flow, config, output plumbing, context management, tools, skills, memory, subagents
papers.proposer: Claude Opus 4.8 as proposer, analyst and critic (also the frozen policy)
papers.signal: Evolve suites: Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks), Harvey LAB (120), EngDesign (61); edit budget annealed, leakage critic, stability floor, cost rule, pruning
papers.heldout: Five out-of-distribution benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, JobBench, GDPval, APEX-Agents, Frontier-Eng) and 40 held-out Harvey tasks
papers.result: Evolve-suite gains +1.1 to +6.0; out of distribution +1.8 to +4.7 (best of five; mean 3.6), each within about one standard error; unregularised evolution 92.8 on its evolve split but 40.3 out of distribution; 2.42M tokens per trial against 3.80M (36% fewer, Table 2; the abstract says 30%), still +55% over the unevolved 1.56M
papers.transfer: Released records give +0.9 on Harvey held out where the paper prints +2.3
papers.hack: The critic returned 8 first drafts, 4 for leakage such as a hard-coded task id
papers.toy: Replay the released runs tab; keep-the-best against RRSI's rules toy in Reading

papers.name: SoL-Pi
papers.changes: Token-saving extensions to the Pi harness: 4 kept of 152 directions (observation packing, action fusion, an evidence-preserving reducer, online compaction)
papers.proposer: An auto-research loop driven by GPT-5.6 Sol
papers.signal: 535 search environments; capability must stay within tolerance, then efficiency must improve; acceptance on 11 EdgeBench tasks
papers.heldout: EdgeBench (which includes the 11 acceptance tasks) and Opus 5, a model the search never used
papers.result: 44.7 to 49.0% fewer tokens at 93.7 to 94.3% of Pi's score; about 96% of the traffic is cache reads, so cost fell about 33%
papers.hack: None reported; the search's own cost (over 3,000 runs) not reported

papers.name: Prime Agent
papers.changes: Versioned prompt notes, memories, skills and subagent specs on top of an immutable base prompt
papers.proposer: The agent itself, or a background refine call over trajectory events
papers.signal: No explicit search score: refinement from trajectory evidence
papers.result: 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3 public set (best of 3 runs: 95.0, 95.2, 95.5) against 30% for Opus 5 in the official harness, a number the paper did not run; community harnesses had already posted 98.97 to 100%
papers.transfer: Nothing ablated: no experiment isolates a gain from refinement
papers.hack: In Factorio the agent spawned resources through RCON commands despite an anti-cheating heartbeat, then saved the shortcut as a reusable skill

papers.name: StateM
papers.changes: A YAML runbook of states, transitions, hooks and checks around a fixed CLI agent; failures become new runbook versions
papers.proposer: A hyper-agent (GPT-5.5 in Codex) under human-set rules
papers.signal: Failure traces on the same 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks it is scored on
papers.result: GPT-5.5 83.1% to 92.1% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, same weights: a development-set number
papers.transfer: The leaderboard judge flagged 13 of 424 rewarded trajectories (9 possible reward hacking, 4 harness cheating); zeroing them gives 92.36%; the PR was closed unmerged
papers.hack: Task-shaped gates; the authors disclose two ways the hyper-agent learned the benchmark rather than the task
papers.toy: Replay a real StateM run tab

papers.name: NeoHorse-1
papers.org: TokenRhythm with Tsinghua, PKU, CUHK, Alibaba and others
papers.changes: Model weights, through a curriculum ordered by a routing harness's signals (SFT plus on-policy distillation)
papers.proposer: A fixed, unnamed teacher; the router's tiers order the data
papers.signal: A six-dimension judge plus structural gates
papers.heldout: Ten benchmarks; two run in the very harness whose traffic was the training data
papers.result: Qwen3.5-4B 58.94 to 64.87 macro over ten benchmarks; the controlled harness-data comparison is +1.26 (Table 3)
papers.transfer: The evaluate, select, update loop ran once: compounding untested
papers.seeds: 3 runs on three benchmarks, 1 on two
papers.toy: Schedule the curriculum tab; a loss-mask widget in Reading

papers.name: Dream-RSI
papers.changes: The exploration policy's code (which branches to pursue, batch width, when to stop), scored offline by replay over recorded search trees
papers.proposer: A development agent (a fixed, unnamed model)
papers.signal: Replay score: best revealed score minus a per-attempt charge plus a batching bonus
papers.heldout: Search on 17 synthetic Lasso instances, results on 6 real held-out datasets
papers.result: Calls 550 to 317 with Gemini-3.1-Pro; but the solver is faster than the fixed baseline on only 1 of 6 datasets (13% slower on the geometric mean)
papers.transfer: Replay is valid only inside the recorded history
papers.toy: Dream over a recorded tree tab

env_papers.name: Terminal-Universe
env_papers.what: Rebuilds workspaces from 359,593 recorded trajectories (replay, agentic completion, LLM sufficiency judge); 37,273 kept, judged task-sufficient by an LLM, not shown runnable; completion writes 87% of files
env_papers.result: Qwen3.5-27B SFT: Terminal-Bench 2.1 46.2 to 58.1; re-solving recovered tasks 52.1 against imitating the source trajectories 36.7 (below the base 47.0)
env_papers.caveat: Gain is distillation from Qwen3.7-Max as much as environments; 96.3% from one corpus

env_papers.name: EnvHarness
env_papers.what: Wraps an existing environment at its reset/step interface (Stage, Contract, Rules, Chain), keeps its verifier; accepts a wrapper when K rollouts land in a 0.4 to 0.6 success band
env_papers.result: ALFWorld out of distribution 70.4 against 61.4; SWE-bench Verified 214 against 203 of 407
env_papers.caveat: 3 runs per arm; only 3 of 14 gains reach p<0.05; contracts fake some environment behaviour

env_papers.name: DSec
env_papers.what: DeepSeek's sandbox infrastructure for agentic RL: about 3 million sandboxes a day on about 160 nodes, peak about 380K concurrent, over 5,000 created per second (self-reported)
env_papers.result: Sandboxes read only 4.2 to 13.3% of an image
env_papers.caveat: Agents searched platform logs for answers, forged RPC requests, overwrote /bin/bash, and one used a filesystem ioctl to get around AppArmor; the sandbox is a reward-hacking mitigation, not claimed inescapable
